seed_draft: We study Hadamard matrices of order n whose entries are l-th roots of unity. A main problem is to determine the allowed pairs (n,l). Write l = p_1^{a_1}...p_s^{a_s}. We discuss the necessary condition that n lies in p_1 N + ... + p_s N. For s=1 the statement is a classical fact. For s=2 and s=3 we prove it in this paper. For s>=4 we state it as a conjecture. We also comment on other known obstructions to existence.
notes: Seed must be written from v1 abstract; the s=1 case is flagged as known in v1 already, so the claim is s=2,3. Authors withdrew themselves (author-as-community).

seed_draft: We propose a generalisation of the Cameron-Erdos conjecture for sum-free sets to linear equations over the integers in three or more variables that are not translation invariant. The extremal solution-free sets for this class were already known in size. Our argument bounds the number of independent sets of the associated graphs.

seed_draft: Given a family of convex objects in R^d whose maximum independent set (pairwise disjoint subfamily) has size at most m, how many axis-parallel hyperplanes are needed to meet every member? We show this number T_d(m) exists and depends only on m and d. We give a first super-exponential bound, then a polynomial bound in m for fixed d. In the plane we improve the best known exponential bound to O(m^2).
notes: Owner names appear only in the later withdrawn abstract (v4), not in v1; use v1. Under a different name = good test of vocabulary stripping.

seed_draft: We generalize the wedge product of association schemes to table algebras. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for a table algebra to be the wedge product of two table algebras. When the duals of two commutative table algebras are table algebras, we show the dual of their wedge product is a table algebra isomorphic to the wedge product of the duals in reverse order. We close with applications to association schemes.

seed_draft: We use the Rasiowa-Sikorski lemma on generic filters for countable Boolean algebras to build a model of Peano arithmetic from forcing-style conditions. We show that in the resulting standard model the twin prime conjecture holds, i.e. there are infinitely many primes p with p+2 prime. The argument assigns to each arithmetic sentence a Boolean value and uses a countable family of dense sets to force the statement. A companion paper uses the same method to show infinitely many Mersenne primes.

citation: Campos, Griffiths, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, An exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey, Annals of Math. 203(3) (2026) 869-932, DOI 10.4007/annals.2026.203.3.4

community_evidence.summary: Annals publication; abstract: 'first exponential improvement' over Erdos-Szekeres 1935. Later source: Morris survey arXiv:2601.05221 (snippet).

seed_draft: We show that the diagonal Ramsey number R(k) satisfies R(k) <= (4 - eps)^k for some absolute constant eps > 0 and all large k. The Erdos-Szekeres bound of 1935 has stood as the exponential rate since then. We obtain the improvement via a book algorithm, a density-increment-like procedure that finds large monochromatic books in a two-coloured complete graph. A careful analysis of the algorithm's steps bounds the number of 'bad' steps.
notes: Test of false-kill on a famous result; model may recall it. Not post-cutoff.

seed_draft: The bunkbed conjecture of Kasteleyn (1985) asserts that in a graph G times K_2 with independent edge percolation, a vertex u in the lower copy is at least as likely to connect to v in the upper copy as to the lower copy of v. We give a counterexample on a planar graph with 7222 vertices. The construction converts a small hypergraph counterexample into an ordinary graph through a gadget, and the probability gap is computed exactly. The gap is about 10^-6509.
notes: Seed contains construction details from the abstract; remove Hollom reference.

seed_draft: We treat non-locality and contextuality in one framework by taking empirical models to be presheaf-like families of distributions over measurement contexts.
